tips: Use @ to attach files like @src/main.rs.
Use @! for hidden or ignored files: @!.github/workflows.
Press Ctrl+O to toggle auto-approve mode.
Use Shift+Tab to cycle between modes like Plan mode.
Run /compact [context] when chat gets long.
Press Ctrl+B to background a running terminal command.
Start Grok in a fresh worktree with `-w`; add `-r <session-id>` to resume an existing session there.
Use Ctrl+Enter to interject messages. Or just Enter to queue messages.
Run /dashboard (or Ctrl+\) to see and manage all your agents in one place.
Try out workflows using /workflows.

availableCommands.description: Drive a running Amaro instance from Claude Code using the `amaro` CLI. Use when the user wants to inspect data apps / connectors / cache / chat sessions, run a data app, drive the running desktop UI, or stream telemetry. Triggers on mentions of "amaro CLI", "amaro app", "drive amaro", "amaro headless", "amaro mcp", or "list data apps".
availableCommands.name: amaro

availableCommands.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
availableCommands.name: find-skills

availableCommands.description: Claim and execute queued Elk 'Do' runs waiting for this machine's Claude Code executor. Use when the user says pick up / pull / drain / check Elk work, or runs /elk-inbox. Loops claim_run → do the work → report_progress heartbeats → submit_deliverable.
availableCommands.name: elk-inbox

availableCommands.description: Pre-weave a session locally before filing it to Elk: read the workspace's List and goals first, dedupe against open actions, resolve finished work to action ids, then emit ONE structured capture. Use whenever capturing / saving / filing a session or milestone to Elk — i.e. in place of any bare capture_to_elk call, including the running captures a project's CLAUDE.md asks for.
availableCommands.name: elk-preweave

availableCommands.description: any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) to knowledge graph. Use when user asks any question about a codebase, documents, or project content - especially if graphify-out/ exists, treat the question as a /graphify query.
availableCommands.name: graphify

availableCommands.description: Execute a PR Plan DAG from a design document. Parses the plan, topologically sorts it, implements PRs in parallel using worktree-isolated subagents, runs mandatory orchestrator-level review, and assembles either a Graphite PR stack or a plain-git branch stack depending on tool availability.
availableCommands.name: execute-plan

availableCommands.description: Prompting and workflow guidance for Imagine image tools
availableCommands.name: bundled:imagine

availableCommands.description: Run the full implement-review-fix loop using implementer and reviewer personas. Supports effort-based multi-reviewer scaling (1-5 reviewers) with automatic specialization selection. Includes memory-based feedback loop that learns from past review patterns. Loops until all reviewers find 0 issues of any severity.
availableCommands.name: implement

availableCommands.description: Monitor PRs, fix CI failures, address review comments, resolve merge conflicts, and restack stacks. Supports independent PRs, Graphite stacks, and GitHub stacked PRs (gh-stack).
